summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Capacitation occurs in female tract (5-6h: cholesterol removal, motility hyperactivation). Acrosomal reaction: ZP3 binding -> Hyaluronidase & Acrosin release. Prevention of Polyspermy: Fast Block (electrical depolarization via Na+ influx, -70 mV to +20 mV for ~60s) vs Slow Block (intracellular Ca2+ wave -> Cortical granule exocytosis cleaves ZP3 and hardens Zona Pellucida). Sperm entry triggers completion of Meiosis II -> Ootid + 2nd polar body.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 6.1 Capacitation & The Acrosomal Reaction
1. **Capacitation**: Physiological conditioning of sperm in the female reproductive tract ($\approx 5\text{--}6\text{ hours}$). Female secretions remove decapacitation factors, cholesterol, and glycoproteins from the acrosomal membrane, increasing permeability to $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ and driving hyperactivated flagellar motility.
2. **Acrosomal Reaction**: Binding of sperm surface galactosyltransferase to the **$\text{ZP}_3$ glycoprotein receptor** triggers acrosomal exocytosis:
   - **Hyaluronidase**: Hydrolyzes hyaluronic acid cementing corona radiata cells.
   - **Acrosin / Corona Penetrating Enzyme**: Serine proteases that digest a path through the Zona Pellucida.

### 6.2 Prevention of Polyspermy: Fast vs. Slow Blocks

```
                        BLOCKS TO POLYSPERMY
                        
   1. FAST BLOCK (Transient):
      Sperm fusion ──► Rapid Na+ Influx ──► Depolarizes Oolemma (-70 mV to +20 mV).
      Prevents further sperm fusion for ~60 seconds.
      
   2. SLOW BLOCK / CORTICAL REACTION (Permanent):
      Depolarization triggers cytosolic Ca2+ Wave from Endoplasmic Reticulum.
      ├── Cortical Granules undergo exocytosis into the Perivitelline Space.
      ├── Granular enzymes cleave ZP3 receptors (destroying sperm binding).
      └── Cross-links ZP glycoproteins, hardening the Zona Pellucida into a Fertilization Envelope.
```

conceptBreakdown.heading: Cytosolic Calcium Wave Mechanics
conceptBreakdown.title: Cytosolic Calcium Wave Mechanics
conceptBreakdown.content: Sperm introduces a soluble phospholipase C zeta (PLC-zeta) into the egg cytoplasm, generating IP3 which binds IP3 receptors on the endoplasmic reticulum, releasing waves of Ca2+ that activate cortical granule exocytosis and restart the cell cycle.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Metaphase II Anaphase-Promoting Complex Activation
conceptBreakdown.title: Metaphase II Anaphase-Promoting Complex Activation
conceptBreakdown.content: The Ca2+ surge activates the Anaphase-Promoting Complex (APC/C), which degrades cyclin B and Securin, permitting separase to cleave cohesins and allowing the secondary oocyte to complete anaphase II.
